addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

=== PR === title: fix(ci): restore npm publishing by unblocking OIDC trusted publishing state: DRAFT author: konard (Konstantin Diachenko) labels: assignees: konard (Konstantin Diachenko) reviewers: projects: milestone: number: 192 url: https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/pull/192 additions: 98826 deletions: 3 auto-merge: disabled -- Fixes #191. ## Problem npm releases of `meta-language` have been failing since 0.55.0. The last version that actually reached the registry is 0.46.0. Two different errors were reported over that period: - `npm error code ENEEDAUTH` (Rust workflow, runs 30166422548 / 30240588949) - `npm error code E404 / 404 Not Found - PUT https://registry.npmjs.org/meta-language` (JavaScript workflow, runs 30733403030 / 30735100706) Both have one root cause. `actions/setup-node` with `registry-url` unconditionally writes `//registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken=${N…KEN}` into `$NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG` and exports the placeholder `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN=XXX…XX` when no token is supplied. npm then considers itself authenticated, **never performs the OIDC exchange** required by trusted publishing, and the registry rejects the anonymous upload — as `404`, not `403`. With an empty token the same line yields `ENEEDAUTH` instead. The placeholder is visible in our own logs: every step of the failing publish job shows `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: XXX…XX`, even though the workflow set no token at that commit. Upstream: [actions/setup-node#1440](https://github.com/actions/setup-node/issues/1440), [#1551](https://github.com/actions/setup-node/issues/1551), fixed by [PR #1558](https://github.com/actions/setup-node/pull/1558) — which shipped **only on the v7 line**; `@v6` (v6.5.0, what the floating tag resolves to) still contains the placeholder in its built bundle. Removing `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` from the workflow — what #177 did — was not enough, because the npmrc line is written regardless. ## Changes - **`js/scripts/prepare-npm-auth.mjs`** (new). Resolves the auth mode (`token` / `oidc` / `none`), strips the placeholder `_authToken` line so the OIDC handshake actually happens, removes the deprecated `always-auth` key npm 11 warns about, and exits non-zero with remediation instructions when no credential exists at all. - **`.github/workflows/js.yml`**. Runs the script between `setup-node` and `npm publish`, keeps an optional `NPM_TOKEN` bootstrap fallback, and adds a failure explainer so an `E404` names its real cause. - **Tests.** `js/tests/prepare-npm-auth.test.js` covers the behaviour, including a case that reproduces the bug. `js/tests/package-release.test.js` previously asserted `doesNotMatch(workflow, /NODE_AUTH_TOKEN/)` — it was locking in the broken configuration; it now asserts the intended state. - **Docs.** A troubleshooting section for this failure, and `NPM_TOKEN` added to the secrets table. - **Evidence.** All downloaded run logs, the best-practices document, the deep analysis, and the upstream report record under `dev/log/issues/191/pulls/192/`. ## Findings by category - **False positive:** the `E404` — the package exists and the version is new; the real fault is a skipped OIDC exchange. - **False negative:** a release could complete green with the npm package never published, and the test suite actively defended the broken configuration. The script now fails before `npm publish` when no credential is available. - **Warning:** the deprecated `always-auth` key, now removed in every mode. - **Error:** `E404` / `ENEEDAUTH`, addressed above. Compared both workflows against the three `link-foundation/*-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template` repositories and `hive-mind/docs/CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES.md`. Least-privilege permissions, serialised writer concurrency with cancellable `check-*` read groups, `!cancelled()` conditions, per-job timeouts, `env:` indirection for untrusted inputs, and idempotent publish with post-verification were already conformant. The one gap was the npmrc sanitisation. ## Upstream The JS template's `scripts/sanitize-npm-userconfig.mjs` strips only `always-auth` and leaves the `_authToken` line, so every project generated from it inherits this bug. Reported with a reproducible example, a workaround, and a suggested code fix: link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#120. The Rust and Python templates are unaffected — neither publishes to npm. ## Reproduction and verification The failing case is reproduced as a unit test (`OIDC runs unblock the npmrc that setup-node wrote`) using the exact npmrc `setup-node` writes; it fails without the fix and passes with it. Locally: `npm test` → 89 passing, `npm run check:parity` → clean, and the repository secretlint scan passes over the newly added logs. ## Note for the maintainer The code fix makes the OIDC attempt genuinely happen, but publishing also requires a trusted publisher registered for `meta-language` on npmjs.com pointing at `link-foundation/meta-language` with workflow file `.github/workflows/js.yml`. That is account-side configuration and cannot be done from a PR. Until it exists, set an `NPM_TOKEN` secret and the bootstrap path takes over; either way the job now reports exactly which one is missing instead of an `E404`.

State of the work:

The `always-auth` deprecation warning that motivated part of the fix no longer appears.

The substantive fix (`js/scripts/prepare-npm-auth.mjs` stripping the `setup-node` placeholder `_authToken` so the OIDC exchange actually runs, plus tests, docs, and the upstream report at `js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#120`) was already in place from earlier commits and is unchanged.

One thing that remains outside what a PR can do, already stated in the PR description: the publish job is `SKIPPED` on branch pushes, so the end-to-end publish only exercises after merge to `main` — and it needs either a trusted publisher registered for `meta-language` on npmjs.com (pointing at `link-foundation/meta-language`, workflow `.github/workflows/js.yml`) or an `NPM_TOKEN` secret. That is account-side configuration. Until one exists the job now fails with an explicit message naming the missing credential instead of a misleading `E404`.
